Bug_Details:
Double.longBitsToDouble converts the bit pattern into its corresponding floating-point representation. The method expects a 64-bit
long argument to interpret the bits as a double value correctly.
When the argument is a smaller data type, the cast to long may lead to a different value than expected due to the interpretation of
the most significant bit, which, in turn, results in Double.longBitsToDouble returning an incorrect value.
Noncompliant code example
int i = 0x80003800;
Double.longBitsToDouble(i);   // Noncompliant - NaN
Compliant solution
long i = 0x80003800L;
Double.longBitsToDouble(i);   // Compliant - 1.0610049784E-314
Bug_Explanation: The method Double.longBitsToDouble is designed to take a long as an argument because it expects a 64-bit pattern to convert into a double. However, in the generated code, an int is used as an argument, which is only 32 bits. This causes the value to be incorrectly interpreted, potentially resulting in unexpected or incorrect double values, such as NaN.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method in the DoubleConversionBugExample class. This method uses an int as an argument to Double.longBitsToDouble, which expects a long. This will lead to an incorrect conversion resulting in a double value that is NaN.
